text_blocks.snippet: HIV significantly weakens the immune system by targeting and destroying CD4 T cells, which are crucial for fighting off infections. This destruction leads to a compromised immune response, making the body vulnerable to opportunistic infections and other illnesses.
snippet_highlighted_words: HIV significantly weakens the immune system by targeting and destroying CD4 T cells

list.snippet: HIV primarily infects and destroys CD4 T cells, also known as helper T cells, which are essential for coordinating the immune response.
These cells signal other immune cells to attack pathogens, so their depletion leaves the body vulnerable.

text_blocks.snippet: 2. The Process of Immune System Damage

list.snippet: HIV uses CD4 cells to replicate itself, essentially turning them into viral factories that produce more HIV particles.
As HIV replicates, it kills the infected CD4 cells, leading to a decline in their numbers.
This continuous destruction of CD4 cells weakens the overall immune response, making the body susceptible to infections.
